items.content:
Halloween 2026: Twitch Drops & Content Creator Cats!

Halloween is here, and we're bringing two ways to add some new feline friends to your HQ in The Other Side!

Twitch Drops | Hex Cat

Earn the exclusive Hex Cat by watching participating Twitch streams during our Halloween 2026 Twitch Drops campaign!

To get started, you'll need to connect your Twitch account to The Other Side.

How to Connect Your Twitch Account to The Other Side!

We're introducing Twitch Drops to The Other Side! Players will now be able to earn exclusive in-game rewards by watching participating Twitch Streams!

Before you can start earning rewards, you'll need to link your Twitch account to your The Other Side account.

Step 1: Launch The Other Side

  • Open The Other Side through Steam.

    [/*]

  • Navigate to the Twitch App in your in-game Laptop.

    [/*]

  • Select Connect on the top right of the window.

    [/*]

Step 2: Authorize Your Twitch Account

  • Navigate Twitch's activation website or press the quick access button.

    [/*]

  • Input the device code provided to you in the connect screen in-game.

    [/*]

  • Follow the prompts to authorize the connection.

    [/*]

Step 3: Confirm Your Connection

  • Return to The Other Side. DO NOT CLICK CANCEL. Allow a few moments for Twitch to connect.

    [/*]

  • Verify that your Twitch account shows as Connected.

    [/*]

  • You're all set! Your account is now ready to receive Twitch Drop rewards.

    [/*]

Step 4: Watch & Earn!

  • Head over to Twitch and find a participating streamer playing The Other Side with Drops enabled.

    [/*]

  • Watch for the required amount of time to earn rewards.

    [/*]

  • Track your progress through your Twitch Drops & Rewards Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Once you've earned a reward, visit your Twitch inventory to claim it.

    Twitch Drops Inventory:

    https://www.twitch.tv/drops/inventory

    [/*]

Step 5: Where to find your new in-game item(s).

  • Head to your in-game Headquarters, and open your Tablet (TAB).

    [/*]

  • Under Home Base, click "Twitch Drops".

    [/*]

  • That's it!

    [/*]

Important Information

  • You must link your accounts to receive in-game Twitch Drop rewards.

    [/*]

  • Only participating streams with Drops enabled will count toward your progress.

    [/*]

  • Rewards must be claimed through your Twitch Drops Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Make sure you're watching on the same Twitch account you've connected to The Other Side.

    [/*]

Content Creator Cats | Adopt a Feline Friend!

Our Content Creator pet adoption feature is back!

Similar to our previous Easter Bunny event, players can adopt a feline companion by joining a Content Creator's lobby.

Here's how it works:

  • Join a participating Content Creator's lobby.

    [/*]

  • Locate their Pet Cat Kennel.

    [/*]

  • Interact with the kennel to adopt your very own cat!

    [/*]

    These cats are earned directly in-game and do not require Twitch Drops or Twitch account linking.

    Two Ways to Earn, More Feline Friends!

    Whether you're watching your favorite streamers to earn the exclusive Hex Cat or joining Content Creators to adopt a cat, there's more than one way to bring home a new companion this Halloween!

This update brings several fixes, quality-of-life improvements, and additional content to our ongoing Halloween Event, Thinning of the Veil.

Fixes

  • Addressed performance issues affecting the new Halloween Headquarters.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several crashes related to the laptop interface and various UI transitions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing all locations to appear as active Halloween Event maps, regardless of the current event rotation. Map rotations are now in order, as seen on our previous Event News page.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Protective Fire: The HQ's protective fire will now turn purple upon completing the Halloween Event progression, providing a visual indication of your accomplishment.

    [/*]

  • Leaderboard Updates: Halloween Event leaderboard scores will now update immediately after Protective Crystals are added to the HQ fire.

    [/*]

  • Time of Day: Added Time of Day adjustments to your new HQ - this will allow the host to pick the time of day, to create the ambience they're looking for.

  • Trick-or-Treating Indicator: Hosts can now enable or disable a Trick-or-Treating icon for their lobby in the Session Browser. Players currently on a Trick-or-Treating cooldown will see the icon faded, making it easier to identify available opportunities at a glance.

    [/*]

Halloween Event

  • Added additional unlockable rewards for the Thinning of the Veil Halloween Event in the Cosmetic portion of the Laptop Shop. These include: - 4 female and 3 male costume unlocks - 2 Halloween Box Truck Skins - Unisex "Boo-ty" pants - 2 Halloween 2026 Hoodies

    [/*]

  • Added additional unlockable rewards from last year's Halloween Event in the Collectors Vault

    [/*]

Thank You!

Thank you to everyone who has participated in Thinning of the Veil so far!

We've loved seeing everyone investigate, perform rituals, collect crystals, and work toward unlocking their Halloween rewards.

We'll continue monitoring feedback and addressing issues throughout the event.

Happy Halloween, Investigators!

The Other Side Team

items.title: HALLOWEEN EVENT - Thinning of the Veil
items.summary: Halloween 2026: Thinning of the Veil October 22 - November 3 The veil between the living and the dead is growing thinner, and something sinister is creeping into The Other Side . This Halloween, we're introducing an all-new seasonal event f
items.content:
Halloween 2026: Thinning of the Veil

October 22 - November 3

The veil between the living and the dead is growing thinner, and something sinister is creeping into The Other Side.

This Halloween, we're introducing an all-new seasonal event featuring rituals, protective crystals, trick-or-treating, exclusive cosmetics, and a brand-new seasonal HQ that you get to keep forever!

Whether you're hunting ghosts, collecting candy, or working to keep the darkness at bay, there's plenty to uncover this Halloween.

Your New Seasonal Headquarters

Every player will receive a brand-new Halloween Headquarters, completely free!

But there's a catch... something sinister is lurking beyond the safety of your HQ, and the only thing keeping it away is the light.

Throughout the event, you'll collect Protective Crystals to strengthen your HQ's protective fire, gradually illuminating your surroundings and unlocking new lighting decorations along the way.

The more crystals you collect, the brighter your HQ becomes!

And yes, your Halloween HQ and the lighting decorations you unlock are yours to keep, even after the event ends.

Rituals & Protective Crystals

This year, we're bringing a new kind of Halloween experience into your contracts.

Upon entering an event contract, you'll discover a Ritual Table, accompanied by instructions detailing how to complete the ritual.

Your task? Gather the necessary ritual items and perform the ritual to obtain Protective Crystals.

Here's how it works:

  • Prepare the Ritual Table. Follow the instructions provided to set up your ritual.

    [/*]

  • Find the Ritual Bones. Search the location for four different bones hidden throughout the environment. These can be found both indoors and outdoors. Listen carefully for faint whispers and watch for their purple glow!

    [/*]

  • Perform the Ritual. Place the bones into their corresponding bowls to activate the ritual and reveal your rewards. 

    [/*]

  • Collect Your Crystals. Gather the Protective Crystals from the ritual bowls and place them into your crystal pouch.

    [/*]

  • Complete Your Contract. You'll need to successfully finish your contract to bring your collected crystals home!

    [/*]

    Once you've returned to your HQ, take your crystal pouch to the protective fire and toss it in.

    Watch as your fire grows stronger, pushing back the darkness and illuminating more of your surroundings!

    Larger maps offer additional opportunities to perform rituals, and your contract difficulty multiplier can influence your chances of receiving bonus crystals.

    Keep collecting crystals to unlock all of the seasonal HQ lighting sets and, for our most dedicated investigators, the exclusive Halloween Trophy!

    Trick or Treat!

    What's Halloween without a little trick-or-treating?

    This year, we're bringing back player-to-player Trick or Treating, allowing you to visit other players' lobbies and collect candy!

    Players hosting lobbies will have candy buckets available for visitors. Hosts will need to periodically refill their buckets to keep the treats flowing, so don't forget to check yours!

    But trick-or-treating isn't the only way to collect candy.

    Candy buckets can also be found throughout event locations, offering investigators a chance to collect some extra sweets while hunting ghosts.

    Be careful, though! Not every bucket contains a treat...

    Some might have a little trick waiting for you instead. 

    Ritual Rewards & Candy

    Performing rituals isn't just about gathering Protective Crystals.

    Successful rituals can also reward you with candy!

    Unlike the candy buckets scattered throughout the location, candy earned from rituals is always safe. No tricks, no surprises, just something sweet for your efforts.

    🛍️ The Halloween Cosmetic Shop

    All that candy has to go somewhere!

    Throughout the event, you'll be able to spend your collected candy in our seasonal Halloween Shop, featuring a variety of exclusive cosmetics, including:

    •  Halloween Costumes

      [/*]

    •  Halloween Hoodies

      [/*]

    •  Halloween Truck Skins

      [/*]

    The Halloween Shop will open 24 hours after the event begins, giving everyone an opportunity to explore the event, participate in rituals, and collect some candy before the shopping begins!

    Rotating Haunted Locations

    Throughout Thinning of the Veil, Halloween event locations will rotate daily, with different maps available each day.

    This gives investigators an opportunity to explore different locations, perform rituals, and experience the event across a variety of environments.

    On October 31st, ALL Halloween event maps will be available for 36 hours!

    So grab your friends, prepare your equipment, and get ready for a Halloween filled with investigations.

    October 22, 6:00 PM - Oct 23, 6:00 PM CDT Ravenwood / Asylum

    October 23, 6:00 PM - Oct 24, 6:00 PM CDT Cedar / St Joseph's

    October 24, 6:00 PM - Oct 25, 6:00 PM CDT Aspen / Abaddon East

    October 25, 6:00 PM - Oct 26, 6:00 PM CDT Blackmeadow / Cemetery West

    October 26, 6:00 PM - Oct 27, 6:00 PM CDT McGavin / Stone Manor

    October 27, 6:00 PM - Oct 28, 6:00 PM CDT Ravenwood / St Joseph's

    October 28, 6:00 PM - Oct 29, 6:00 PM CDT Cedar / Abaddon East

    October 29, 6:00 PM - Oct 30, 6:00 PM CDT Aspen / Cemetery West

    October 30, 6:00 PM CDT - Nov 1, 5:00 AM CST ALL MAPS (Halloween - 36 Hours)

    November 1, 5:00 AM - 5:00 PM CST Blackmeadow / Stone Manor

    November 1, 5:00 PM - Nov 2, 5:00 PM CST McGavin / Asylum

    November 2, 5:00 PM - Nov 3, 5:00 PM CST Ravenwood / Abaddon East

    November 3, 5:00 PM - Nov 4, 5:00 PM CST Cedar / Cemetery West

    A Trophy Worth Hunting For

    For those willing to brave the darkness, an exclusive Halloween Trophy awaits.

    Collect Protective Crystals throughout the event to unlock your HQ lighting decorations and work toward the ultimate seasonal reward! The trophy is intended for our most dedicated investigators, so you'll need to put your ghost hunting skills to work if you want to earn it!

    The Veil Is Thinning...

    Thinning of the Veil runs from  October 22 through November 3, 2026.

    Your seasonal HQ is waiting, the ritual tables are ready, and the darkness is growing stronger.

    Gather your crystals. Keep the fire burning. And whatever you do...

    Don't let the light go out.

    Happy Halloween, Investigators!

    The Other Side Team

items.title: NEW TRAINER LOBBIES
items.summary: We hear you, and we don't disagree. Our current tutorial is lacking, to say the least , and improving the new-player experience is something we're actively prioritizing. For that reason, our existing tutorial is receiving a complete overhau
items.content:
We hear you, and we don't disagree. Our current tutorial is lacking, to say the least, and improving the new-player experience is something we're actively prioritizing.

For that reason, our existing tutorial is receiving a complete overhaul and will be replaced with a new, easy-to-follow, killhouse-style tutorial designed to walk players through the game's mechanics, the cellphone, equipment, and systems in a much more comprehensive and approachable way. The new tutorial will also be multiplayer, so you and your friends can learn together!

In the interest of transparency, we had originally hoped to have this ready by the end of next week. However, with our Halloween Event just 11 days away, we're focusing on making sure everything is ready for the event before shifting our full attention back to the tutorial overhaul. We expect to have the new tutorial available within the next few weeks.

In the meantime, we've introduced TRAINER LOBBIES!

You can find these lobbies by selecting the "Training" filter in the session browser.

Our Trainers are trusted members of the community who have demonstrated exceptional game knowledge, patience, and a genuine passion for helping others learn.

Whether you're a brand-new player trying to get your bearings, a returning player looking for a refresher, or an experienced investigator hoping to sharpen your skills, these lobbies are an excellent resource.

We recognize that learning the game shouldn't require outside assistance, and our goal is to make sure the new tutorial reflects that. Until then, we encourage anyone looking for guidance to take advantage of the Trainer Program.

To find a Trainer Lobby: Head over to your Laptop, and navigate to the MULTIPLAYER button, then click "FIND"

On the left side of your screen, you'll see "FILTERS: In Contract / Full / Trainer Only" Check mark "Trainer Only" to see all available sessions.

If a trainer is online, their lobby will clearly say "TRAINER" in the session browser

Don't see a trainer online? Head over to our Discord, and @Trainer role. They're volunteers, and aren't always on the game - but someone is always in the Discord! We appreciate your patience, your feedback, and your continued support as we work to make The Other Side better.

items.summary: Two New Haunted Locations Have Arrived in The Other Side BLACK MEADOW FARMS Explore Black Meadow Farms , a secluded farmhouse that has remained in the same family since its earliest days. Something has changed within its walls, and the prop
items.content:
Two New Haunted Locations Have Arrived in The Other Side

BLACK MEADOW FARMS

Explore Black Meadow Farms, a secluded farmhouse that has remained in the same family since its earliest days. Something has changed within its walls, and the property is now plagued by an increasingly aggressive presence.

Black Meadow Farms features:

  • New ghost models

    [/*]

  • New Death Rooms

    [/*]

  • New Artifacts

    [/*]

  • New interactions

    [/*]

  • New throwable objects

    [/*]

THE McGAVIN HOUSE

Step inside The McGavin House, a historically preserved estate dating back to the 1800s.

Much of the home has been carefully maintained to reflect the lives of those who once occupied it, but not everything left behind is part of the exhibit.

McGavin House features:

  • New ghost models

    [/*]

  • New Death Rooms

    [/*]

  • New Artifacts

    [/*]

  • New interactions

    [/*]

  • New throwable objects

    [/*]

EXPANDED GHOST INTERACTIONS

Ghosts now have even more ways to interact with the environment.

We've added new throwable objects across every location, giving ghosts a wider variety of objects to disturb, move, and throw during investigations.

Additional throwable objects have been added to:

  • Ravenwood

    [/*]

  • Summerhill Psychiatric

    [/*]

  • Stone Manor

    [/*]

  • Cedar

    [/*]

  • Aspen

    [/*]

  • Abaddon East

    [/*]

  • Abaddon West

    [/*]

Throwables have also received new sound effects, making environmental disturbances feel more distinct and helping players recognize activity happening elsewhere in the location.

NEW & REVAMPED INTERACTIONS

We've added a variety of new environmental interactions across our locations while also revisiting many of the interactions already in the game.

Several existing interactions have been updated to provide clearer visual feedback when a ghost interacts with them.

For example, objects such as radios now provide a visible light indication when they have been activated rather than relying solely on sound.

These changes are intended to make ghost activity easier to recognize for Deaf and hard-of-hearing players, while also making environmental interactions clearer for everyone.

GRAPHICS SCALABILITY

We've expanded graphics scalability options to give players greater control over how The Other Side looks and performs across a wider range of hardware.

Several visual features can now scale more effectively based on your graphics settings, allowing lower-end systems to reduce demanding visual effects while higher-end systems can retain the full visual experience.

This is part of our continued work toward improving performance, accessibility, and hardware compatibility without compromising the atmosphere that makes The Other Side what it is.

AND MORE...

Alongside the larger additions in this update, we've continued polishing environmental interactions, sounds, performance, and location details throughout The Other Side.

With Blackmeadow and The McGavin House now open for investigation, there are more places to explore, more objects for ghosts to interact with, and more ways for the environment itself to give you clues that something is nearby.

WHAT'S NEXT?

Following this update, we're moving full speed ahead on a complete overhaul of The Other Side's tutorial.

The current tutorial will be replaced with a new Killhouse-style training experience designed to provide much clearer, hands-on guidance through the game's mechanics, equipment, and investigation process, including proper use of the cellphone and its features.

Rather than simply introducing the basics, the new tutorial is being designed as a place where players can learn, practice, and hone specific investigation skills before putting them to use in the field.

The new tutorial will also support multiplayer.

You'll be able to enter the training environment with friends, allowing experienced Investigators to help newer players learn the game or giving groups a place to practice specific mechanics together.

And, of course, Halloween is approaching.

The Other Side Halloween Event "Thinning of the veil" will run from October 22nd through November 3rd.

This event is largely based around the belief that during Halloween/Samhain, the veil between the living and the dead becomes thinner, and pulls inspiration from The Dumb Supper, Samhain bonfires, and more.

Of course, we will be brining back the classic lobby-to-lobby trick or treating, as well as a new Headquarters, cosmetics, furniture items, and more for players to unlock during the event!

We'll have more to share about what awaits you as we get closer.

items.summary: Find all 10 Halloween ghosts in GTA Online with timed locations, both ordinary spawn positions and the final Ghosts Exposed jacket unlock.
items.content:
By Hassan Sajid · Oct 1, 2026 Hands-on guide Completed solo on PC Find all 10 Halloween ghosts in GTA Online with timed locations, both ordinary spawn positions and the final Ghosts Exposed jacket unlock.

Zoom image: All 10 locations for the 2026 Ghosts Exposed hunt, including the alternative positions for ghosts 1-9. In this article

Article Contents Jump to the section you need right now.

How to photograph ghosts and track progress Ghost locations and times at a glance Video Guide Full Ghosts Locations Map Ghost 1 (8 PM to 9 PM) Ghost 2 (9 PM to 10 PM) Ghost 3 (10 PM to 11 PM) Ghost 4 (11 PM to 12 AM) Ghost 5 (1 AM to 2 AM) Ghost 6 (2 AM to 3 AM) Ghost 7 (3 AM to 4 AM) Ghost 8 (4 AM to 5 AM) Ghost 9 (5 AM to 6 AM) Ghost 10 (12 AM to 1 AM) Reward More Halloween activities 16 sections 0 % read In this article

How to photograph ghosts and track progress Ghost locations and times at a glance Video Guide Expand Hide TOC ⌄ Full Ghosts Locations Map Ghost 1 (8 PM to 9 PM) Ghost 2 (9 PM to 10 PM) Ghost 3 (10 PM to 11 PM) Ghost 4 (11 PM to 12 AM) Ghost 5 (1 AM to 2 AM) Ghost 6 (2 AM to 3 AM) Ghost 7 (3 AM to 4 AM) Ghost 8 (4 AM to 5 AM) Ghost 9 (5 AM to 6 AM) Ghost 10 (12 AM to 1 AM) Reward More Halloween activities 16 sections 0 % read As part of the 2026 Halloween Update for GTA Online , Rockstar Games has once again added 10 ghosts that appear across Blaine County and Los Santos at specific times during the night. Players can use their in-game phone camera to photograph each spirit and earn cash and RP for every successful capture.

Just like last year's event , the tenth and final ghost only appears once you have photographed all nine previous ghosts. Capturing all ten rewards you with the new Ghosts Exposed Tactical Jacket as a special collectible item.

The ghosts start appearing from 20:00 (8 PM) in-game time, with each one visible for exactly one hour. For example, the first ghost spawns from 8 PM to 9 PM. Ghosts 1-9 each have two different spawn points close to one another within the same area, so make sure to check both spots if you don't see it right away.

The base rewards are GTA$20,000 and 500 RP per ghost, plus GTA$50,000 for completing the set: GTA$250,000 and 5,000 RP altogether. Temporary event bonuses can increase the cash payout; see the Reward section below.

You can start hunting as soon as you receive this message from Ghosts Exposed. Just stay in free roam and you'll eventually get the text.

Zoom image: Ghosts Exposed phone message inviting players to submit paranormal photographs. The text message you'll receive when you are eligible to start the hunt. How to photograph ghosts and track progress Open the camera on your in-game phone and frame the ghost. Take the photograph, then choose Send to Ghosts Exposed ; saving it to your gallery alone is not the submission step. The screenshots below show the send option.

Check the Collectibles section of the Interaction Menu for your Ghosts Exposed progress. The on-screen counter also confirms registered photographs, such as 3/10.

If a ghost is missing, check its time slot first, then both positions pictured for ghosts 1-9. If the slot has passed, return during that ghost's next listed time window. For the final ghost, also check that your counter has reached 9/10.

A flying vehicle is useful for the bridge pylon and church tower. Have it ready before their short time windows rather than spending the slot travelling to collect one.

All times below are in-game time , not your local clock. The ordinary ghosts run from 8 PM to 6 AM, leaving midnight-1 AM for the locked final ghost.

    Specific Ghost: If you select a specific ghost, you are guaranteed to get that ghost. Prefer New: New ghost types have an increased chance of being selected, but not guaranteed. None: All ghost types have an equal chance of being selected.

    • Selecting a specific ghost will not allow you to receive rewards for that game, nor will it unlock the ghost in your guide.

      [/*]
    [/*]

Cellphone

  • Added a Hot Key for the Cellphone Flash (by default, "L")

    [/*]

Ghost Guide

  • Added a Ghost Guide app to the laptop.

    [/*]

  • Players can now view both locked and unlocked ghosts from the Ghost Guide.

    [/*]

  • Unlocked ghosts will display their name.

    [/*]

  • Locked ghosts will continue to display as "???".

    [/*]

  • The Ghost Guide will now keep track of how many times you've successfully identified each ghost.

    [/*]

Ghost Changes

  • Puca can now copy 12 distinct hunting behaviors from other ghosts during hunts.

    [/*]

HQ

  • Added several new items for players to decorate and customize their HQ.

    [/*]

items.title: Version 0.9.8.1 - Orbs and Apparitions
items.summary: 7 New Ghosts Seven new entities have made their way to The Other Side , each bringing their own behaviors and characteristics to uncover: Ataphoi [/*] Hupia [/*] Marid [/*] Nasnas [/*] Puca [/*] Sluagh [/*] Wiederganger [/*] Ghost Orbs Are
items.content:
7 New Ghosts

Seven new entities have made their way to The Other Side, each bringing their own behaviors and characteristics to uncover:

  • Ataphoi

    [/*]

  • Hupia

    [/*]

  • Marid

    [/*]

  • Nasnas

    [/*]

  • Puca

    [/*]

  • Sluagh

    [/*]

  • Wiederganger

    [/*]

Ghost Orbs Are Here

Ghost Orbs have been added as a brand-new evidence type!

Ghost Orbs are normally invisible to the naked eye and can only be seen using infrared vision, adding another reason to keep an eye on your cameras.

  • Ghost Orbs are normally only visible through infrared vision.

    [/*]

  • Orbs can also be photographed using the cellphone camera flash.

    [/*]

New Remote Camera System

A new remotely viewable camera has been added, giving investigators another way to monitor paranormal activity from a safer distance.

  • Supports both visible light and infrared modes.

    [/*]

  • Infrared mode can be used to spot Ghost Orbs.

    [/*]

  • Camera modes can be changed remotely from the vehicle laptop.

    [/*]

  • Live feeds can be viewed through the Phantom Detect app.

    [/*]

New Equipment: Wireless Camcorder

The new Wireless Camcorder can be mounted directly to a tripod for easier placement and monitoring.

  • The Wireless Camcorder can be mounted to the tripod.

    [/*]

  • The tripod can be picked up and carried while the camera remains attached.

    [/*]

Dynamic Light Detection

Lighting now has a much more direct impact on both players and paranormal activity.

Players are now given a dynamic Light Contribution Score based on how illuminated they actually are, rather than simply whether they are standing inside a room with the lights on.

  • The more illuminated you are, the slower your anxiety increases.

    [/*]

  • Standing directly near a light source provides more protection than simply being somewhere in a lit room.

    [/*]

  • Multiple nearby light sources can contribute to your overall illumination.

    [/*]

  • Your score updates dynamically as you move through the environment or lighting conditions change.

    [/*]

Ghosts can also react to lighting in new ways. Depending on the ghost and the situation, light may now influence its behavior, creating new reasons to consider where you're standing, which lights are active, and how much darkness surrounds you.

Cellphone UI Overhaul

The Phantom Detect app has received a complete UI overhaul!

  • Environmental CCTV cameras can now be viewed directly from the cellphone.

    [/*]

  • Added support for viewing feeds from the new Wireless Camcorder.

    [/*]

  • Redesigned the interface to make navigating between available camera feeds cleaner and easier.

    [/*]

Identifier App

The Identifier app has also received a major visual and information overhaul.

  • The main ghost selection screen now has a much cleaner layout.

    [/*]

  • Ghost information pages now include behavioral information.

    [/*]

  • Behavioral information can be unlocked after successfully identifying that ghost type.

    [/*]

The more ghosts you successfully identify, the more you'll learn about what makes each one unique.

Hunt & Network Improvements

We've made several improvements to synchronization during hunts and other rapidly changing paranormal events.

Photo Synchronization

  • Added time synchronization and lag compensation when taking photos.

    [/*]

  • Photo capture timing is now synchronized between players, helping ensure rapidly changing paranormal events are represented consistently for everyone involved in the capture.

    [/*]

Hunt Flicker Synchronization

  • Added time synchronization and lag compensation to ghost flickering during hunts.

    [/*]

  • Hunt flickers are now synchronized between players, greatly reducing situations where a ghost could appear visible to one player while being invisible to another at the same moment.

    [/*]

Hunt Cooldown

  • Hunt cooldowns are now stopped when a forced hunt is activated after disorientation.

    [/*]

Hunt Lighting

  • Lights that are already off now flicker at a much lower intensity while the ghost is hunting.

    [/*]

Ghost Behavior Adjustments

Behavior adjustments have been made to several existing ghost types:

  • Wisp

    [/*]

  • Strigoi

    [/*]

  • Forgotten

    [/*]

  • Demon

    [/*]

  • Bhoot

    [/*]

Keep an eye out - you may find that some familiar ghosts don't behave quite the way you remember.

Evidence Changes

  • EMF is no longer included as passive evidence in Identify.

    [/*]

Breakers & Lighting

We've made several adjustments to how ghosts interact with the investigation site's electrical system.

  • Adjusted how frequently ghosts interact with the breaker panel.

    [/*]

  • Ghosts can now turn the breaker on.

    [/*]

  • Light switches that were not directly interacted with no longer play their interaction sound when their state changes.

    [/*]

Equipment & Placement

Equipment placement should now feel more natural and predictable.

  • Placing equipment now begins with the item facing toward or away from the player as appropriate.

    [/*]

  • When picking up furniture in the HQ, its existing orientation is now preserved when the placement preview begins.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed the Stopwatch app keybind not working while dead.

    [/*]

  • Fixed players being able to interact with the environment while the cellphone was focused.

    [/*]

  • Players can no longer take photos of UV stains without a UV light/stick present.

    [/*]

Between 7 new ghosts, Ghost Orbs, the Wireless Camcorder, revamped cellphone apps, dynamic lighting, new ghost behaviors, and multiplayer synchronization improvements, there's a lot more to discover during your investigations.

See you on The Other Side!

items.title: Ghost of Yōtei Is Hopefully the Last of Its Kind
items.summary: Ghost of Yōtei is a great "checklist" open world game. Maybe, though, we've had enough of these for now.
items.content:
Just a couple hours into Ghost of Yōtei , the latest PlayStation 5 exclusive from Sucker Punch, I knew exactly how my day-to-day experiences with this game would go. At the start of every session, I identify what main quests are available to me at this time, check my map for any side quests, bounties, or places of interest I haven’t completed yet, and then chart a course for the next hour or so of play.

I hop on my horse, ride across the gorgeous fields and streams at the foot of Mount Yōtei, and start checking off boxes. First, locate an Altar of Reflection so I can unlock a skill point. Then, challenge another swordsman to a fight to the death to unlock a charm. After that, I’ll complete a bounty hunt so I have enough cash for weapon upgrades, and then I’m off to kill a base camp of Saito thugs with relative ease. I’m having a lot of formulaic fun.

With any luck, though, this will be one of the last times I play a game like this.

Ghost of Tsushima (2020) was also fine but formulaic. More Stuff In Ghost of Yōtei — a sequel to 2020’s Ghost of Tsushima — players assume the role of Atsu, a young woman from Ezo, Japan (modern-day Hokkaido) in 1603 who seeks to avenge her parents and brother, all of whom were mercilessly butchered by a renegade militia known as the Yōtei Six. Sucker Punch tells this story through a piecemeal approach: You only see bits of the past at a time, with constant hints that there’s more to what’s going on than Atsu just killing evil men.

Obviously, the kind of narrative backdrop Yōtei presents lends itself well to an open-world video game, where the player can advance through the story at whatever pace they like and in a potentially non-linear manner. Since this revenge tale lacks big-picture urgency, there’s tons of optional side activities as well, all of which add color to the whole experience but mostly exist to beef up Atsu ahead of main quest showdowns through money, skill trees, armor upgrades, and other goodies.

With sharp yet simple combat mechanics and top-notch production values, Ghost of Yōtei offers a comforting, familiar feedback loop: Ride around a big map on your horse, find stuff, kill stuff, buy stuff, upgrade stuff, occasionally talk to people, do main quests, and then back to all the stuff. Progress is easy to attain and even easier to track. It’s a constantly engaging experience, albeit a largely frictionless one as well.

I’m enjoying my time with all this stuff. But it is mostly stuff . Things to do. Boxes to check off.

Checklist games are less about wandering through fantastical lands and happening upon neat things by chance, and more about being told exactly what’s available to you ahead of time and letting you determine how much of it actually interests you.

Boxes Checked I wrote earlier in this piece that I’ve spent several hours playing Ghost of Yōtei , but it would be just as accurate to say I’ve been playing Ghost of Yōtei for nearly two decades. I played Ghost of Yōtei briefly in 2008 when I bought a used copy of the first Assassin’s Creed from GameStop for $15. I played Ghost of Yōtei when I was searching for Riddler trophies in Batman: Arkham City in 2011. I played my favorite version of Ghost of Yōtei in 2022 in the form of God of War: Ragnarök , and I played my least favorite version of Ghost of Yōtei two years earlier in the form of Assassin’s Creed Valhalla .

I love Ragnarök , but it wasn’t exactly brand new. To be crystal clear, I’m not saying all open-world action-adventure experiences are exactly the same. When talking about games that share the same essence found in Yōtei , I’m referring more specifically to what some have called Ubisoft-style games (as they popularized these kinds of worlds with Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry ). Personally, I prefer calling them “checklist” games. Unlike the massive locales found in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim , Red Dead Redemption , Elden Ring , or The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild , checklist games are less about wandering through fantastical lands and happening upon neat things by chance, and more about being told exactly what’s available to you ahead of time and letting you determine how much of it actually interests you.

In some cases, a checklist game will truly respect and value the time of its players with well-written side quests, stunning vistas, and compelling characters. In other instances, the world is just a backdrop for more and more content , with little substance to be found. In either case, the game literally tells you what you can find before you find any of it. As a result, these are worlds centered on specific activities and rewards instead of mystery and spontaneity. The actual vista you find at the end of a shrine climb in Yōtei might amaze you, but you also know the second you see those big gates what kind of gameplay to expect for the next few minutes.

Another map screen with lots of THINGS everywhere Too Much Clarity Open worlds attract players because they present (sometimes literal) mountains of possibility. With checklist games like Ghost of Yōtei , you pretty much know all of the possibilities early on. All the points of interest fall into a specific set of categories. Once you start earning money and grabbing resources, it becomes immediately clear what you can buy or craft. Story quests are longer and have more intricacies than smaller side quests. Every time you get a new weapon, the game explains how and when to use it relative to your other weapons. Everything fits neatly together in a game like Ghost of Yōtei , making for a smooth, seamless gameplay experience with few, if any, surprises.

Now, there’s nothing inherently wrong with these kinds of titles. As a general rule, I don’t find any particular video game genre, mechanic, system, or design philosophy inherently good or bad. The implementation of and context around any single aspect of a game is what matters most.

What’s happened over the years, though, is that the checklist game became the bog standard of AAA development for single-player experiences, and not just for Sony and Ubisoft. Halo Infinite ’s campaign follows a lot of the same principles, and even a masterpiece RPG like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt normalized including a similar array of optional side-content, albeit in a way that raised standards for such an experience.

items.title: What's in a ghost hunting kit? You can check one out of the Birmingham Public Library
items.summary: The kits will be available all year long, not just during Halloween.
items.content:
During Halloween, most have their eyes set on candy, but some hope to lay their eyes on ghosts.

The Birmingham Public Library is taking in part in this spooky season, with a ghost hunting kit that people can check out.

Public Relations Director Roy Williams said the kit has everything you need to catch some ghosts.

“It starts out with what is called an E.M.F. detector. If you take it to a room, turn it on, it will detect whether or not there are any spirits in the room,” stated Williams.

Williams said you'll need proof to show you've caught your ghosts.

“We have a voice recorder and charging cable, and this is bascially where you'll be able to record if you are having any communications with spirits on the other side,”

The kit also includes a flashlight, a spirit board, a pendulum and two books. One is about the basics of ghost hunting and the other is about the haunted history of Birmingham.

“If you want to know about the paranormal and how to communicate with the other side, we have books here, and we also have a lot of activities just to help people celebrate Halloween in a different way this year,” said Williams.

The kits will be available all year long, not just during Halloween. To check them out, click here.

items.content:
Indie Spotlight | Conrad Stevenson's Paranormal P.I. is a detective game with a spooky twist

That's where Conrad Stevenson's Paranormal P.I. comes in. Unlike other games like Phasmophobia , Devour, or Forewarned , my goal here is not to simply identify an entity and scarper before it kills me. Instead, I'm to delve into the stories of each spirit in a longform single-player campaign.

Stepping into Stevenson's shoes as a diehard fan of Phasmophobia's online co-op format was a disarming experience, albeit a fulfilling one. There's no dwindling sanity meter to worry about as I linger in the dark, nor the threat of triggering a deadly hunt with a cursed tarot deck. I can't even bring a friend with me this time. The two games share a first-person perspective and feature many of the same tools, but without the threat of dying on the job, Conrad's adventure is more about helping spirits move on rather than hunting them down.

Indie developer D&A Games has created an authentic paranormal investigation sim that puts storytelling and methodology at the forefront. The key to success? Treating each haunting as an active crime scene.

Conrad Stevenson's Paranormal P.I. begins with a newly-qualified Conrad establishing himself as both an investigator and museum curator. As a single-player game, Conrad Stevenson features more naturalistic touches than the likes of Phasmophobia. I have to check Conrad's emails via his office computer ahead of each mission, waiting to be invited to investigate new locations. Once invited, I then need to use online archives to collect notes that could be useful to me. From title deeds to newspaper clippings, I can collect up to six POIs to jot down before heading to a haunt, and the evidence I collect seems to be influenced by my notetaking.

Station to Station got around my puzzle game ineptitude by appealing to my 30-year obsession with steam

During an investigation, I can carry up to five tools on me at any given time, cycling through them using the number keys on my keyboard. That's about where the Phasmophobia similarities end. Just two hours in, it's clear that Conrad Stevenson requires you to take a more methodical approach to ghost hunting. The identity of the person whose spirit is lingering actually matters, with each achievement relating to specific entities you can exorcize or release over the course of the game. Repeat visits to a location are not only encouraged but necessary; there are multiple ghosts haunting each map, and any evidence you collect or find can be analyzed in Conrad's office to uncover new notes to bring with you next time. The more notes you bring to an investigation, the more likely you are to trigger complex ghost manifestations – and find out how to set them free.

One of the most unique things about Conrad Stevenson's Paranormal P.I. is how the stories of each ghost are revealed. Certain ghost types have relics needed for the release rituals, anchor items keeping them tethered to the mortal plane when they should have moved on. Having only played a couple hours of the game so far I've yet to find my first relic. I'm slowly uncovering the identity of two ghosts haunting the basement and children's bedroom of a spacious bungalow, and though I already suspect one of them is a poltergeist, the chance of finding relics is improved by finding noteworthy evidence.

In the children's bedroom I find a black and white photograph, too blurry to make out much detail. It appears to depict a man and woman on their wedding day, and although it doesn't offer much else immediately, some on-screen text tells me to check my archives when I get back to the office to learn more about it.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

...an incredibly satisfying, often emotional experience, in possibly the most authentic ghost hunting game yet.

These instances of more granular investigation are what set Conrad Stevenson apart from its competitors, requiring me to pore over my findings and piece together not only who the spirit is, but how and why they died. Contrast this with Phasmophobia, where you can ask ghosts silly questions with a ouija board and chip away at your sanity, and Conrad Stevenson feels like a meaningful puzzle game more than an all-out fear fest.

That being said, it's still spooky. Every light flicker puts me on edge, as does the distant creaking of a floorboard on the other side of this empty house, but Conrad Stevenson's Paranormal P.I. is a surprisingly heartfelt detective journey. Fair warning: I've heard that some of these ghosts have very, very bleak backstories. From serial killer victims to former slaves, knowing more about the lives that came before these horrible deaths helps Conrad bring them peace. This compassion for the dead makes for an incredibly satisfying, often emotional experience, in possibly the most authentic ghost hunting game yet.

Not necessarily because of my success, though I’ve had my moments, but rather because I’ve been able to experience so much of the deer hunting world. I grew up in Vermont, had family property in New York and Indiana, and when I was in my mid-twenties, I moved to Montana to become a guide. I’ve been lucky enough to hunt deer in a variety of different states, utilizing a collection of different hunting techniques, allowing me to completely immerse myself in an assortment of different deer-hunting cultures.

I’ve sat in tree stands on the edge of cornfields with my bow, tracked and still hunted big woods bucks across snowy ridges, spotted and stalked muleys and whitetails on the open prairie, and even slipped between small woodlots and open fields with a shotgun, bow, and muzzleloader in middle of suburbia . I’ve been a part of family deer camps , planted food plots and placed stands , taken part of massive deer drives , and hunted and worked with a variety of hardcore backcountry outfitters and guides.

Throughout all this experience, I’ve met deer hunters of every size, shape, and color, each with their own preferences for hunting methods and styles. These men and women come from dozens of different states, and nearly all of them have declared their methods to be the best. All of this has led me to ask a very pertinent question—Which states actually produce the best deer hunters?

Like baseball, bass fishing , and arguing about politics, deer hunting is an American pastime. As the country’s most plentiful big game animal, almost every state in the country has a native deer population. Even states without any, such as Hawaii , have introduced the animals so that its citizens can participate in recreational hunting. This means that almost every hunter out there, from your weekend warriors to your world-class pros, has all cut their teeth in the deer woods at one point or another. That being said, this doesn’t mean everyone who goes out to harass their local buck population is a good deer hunter.

We all know those guys and gals who just seem to half-ass it in the woods. They show up late to camp, roll out of bed at 9 or 10 a.m., and then simply take their gun for a walk down a trail. The thing is that while a lot of these hunters get skunked, in a lot of places these hunters actually manage to kill quite a few nice bucks. On the other side of the coin, we also all know a few hunters who are out the door before everyone else, going father, staying out longer, and simply hunting harder, who still never seem to manage to get a deer . Now we can say that these hunters are simply lucky or unlucky respectively, but what it really comes down to is whether or not these folks are good deer hunters.

Being a good deer hunter isn’t necessarily about hunting harder, nor is it just about knowing a lot about deer behavior, nor is it about carrying a lucky rabbit’s foot in your pocket. Rather it’s a combination of all of those things. Good deer hunters are willing to push themselves a little harder, know how to put themselves in the right place at the right time, and can adapt their hunting strategy to create their own luck. They can pick the perfect spot for a stand, wait patiently on a buck for hours or days, track, still hunt , and stalk . They hunt areas with low deer densities, where the buck-to-doe ratio is completely out of whack, and still manage to take a good buck year after year. You can take a truly good deer hunter, blindfold them and then shove them out of a plane to parachute in on any piece of ground in the country, and they’ll be able to find and kill a buck. While these true masters exist in every state in the country, some certainly have more than others.

Harvest numbers show you a lot about which states have the best deer hunters, though not necessarily in the way you might think. It may seem obvious that the states with the highest number of harvested deer must have the best deer hunters. However, there are a lot of other factors involved. Most states with high deer harvest numbers also have incredibly high populations of deer and are places with good forage and habitat where deer populations can thrive. The simple fact is that in states like this deer hunting becomes easier and consequently it takes less skill to be successful.

One of the regions with the highest success rates in the country is the Midwest. Pennsylvania , Ohio , Indiana , Illinois , and Wisconsin record some of the highest antlered buck harvest rates in the country, with Pennsylvania topping the charts in 2021 with estimates of 145,320 harvested bucks. While this data doesn’t exactly state that good deer hunters don’t come from this region, what it does show is that hunting in the Midwest is simply easier than hunting in areas with lower deer densities. So much so that many hunters from other parts of the country actually travel to different Midwestern states, simply to have an opportunity to shoot a buck they wouldn’t have in their own state.

“I go to Ohio every year because the sound of a snapping twig or the ruffling of the leaves always has me on edge because I might be about to encounter the biggest buck of my life,” avid Vermont and New York deer hunter Adam Shepard said. “That’s why I go to the Midwest. That feeling that any moment I could see and potentially harvest the buck of a lifetime . I’ve hunted Vermont my whole life, and I’ve only gone to Ohio a handful of times, but in that handful, I’ve seen more big bucks there than I have in Vermont in my entire lifetime.”

High harvest numbers also help to eliminate other regions from states with top deer hunters. In the South, states like Georgia , Alabama, Louisiana, and Mississippi show buck harvests between 80,000 and 140,000 animals. Similarly, states like North and South Dakota, Montana , Idaho , Wyoming, Kansas , Oklahoma , Nebraska and Colorado also boast incredibly high success rates for their regions. Of course, when you’re talking about harvest numbers, it’s impossible to leave out Texas . The Lonestar State boasts the highest deer population in the nation with over 5.5 million deer calling it home. Consequently, the second-largest state in the US also boasts the highest harvest numbers in the country with hunters harvesting over 450,000 bucks in 2021 alone.

Of course, none of these numbers necessarily reflect the skills of the hunters that live in these states. I’m sure there are some absolutely fantastic deer hunters that come from all of them. However, what the numbers do show is that these states have high deer densities with states like Mississippi, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin have over 30 deer per square mile. This means that your average deer hunter, possessing only an average set of skills, has a better chance to go to any of these states and consistently kill a buck. While this makes these places fantastic deer hunting states , it doesn’t necessarily mean that these places produce the best hunters. It’s a long-held belief that bad deer hunting makes for better deer hunters.

While all the states in the union can be challenging to hunt for a variety of reasons—from having rough terrain to low deer populations—there are a few that truly stand out. These states all have their own unique sets of challenges for those that hunt them which forces these men and women to become better deer hunters if they want any chance to stock up on venison . Accordingly, the hunters who can consistently kill big bucks in these states are quite possibly the best deer hunters in the country.

The three states that make up northern New England are all lumped together because the hunters from these states there all face the same challenges—wide swaths of thickly forested land with extremely low numbers of deer and a lot of hunting pressure. All three states have some of the lowest deer densities in the country with the northern regions having between 5 to 15 deer per square mile. Additionally, the few deer that live in these states face a lot of hunting pressure with between 50,000 and 150,000 hunters taking to the woods after them every year. This makes finding and harvesting big bucks in northern New England a special challenge, one that consists of covering a lot of ground to find small pockets of deer , giving even the best hunters only one or two opportunities to be successful per season.

“Northern New England challenges a person’s deer hunting skills second to none,” Rodney Elmer, host of the Mountain Deer Podcast and YouTube Channel said. “It’s like a deer desert, but at least in a desert you can walk, you can see forever, and you have plenty of room to shoot. None of that exists here, so you have to be good to be successful, which means hunting hard because nobody seems to come here and show us a better way to get it done.”
